job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today my father explained why we must be careful with money. He showed me two loan offers for a new bike. One bank uses a flat rate of 8%, while the other uses a reducing-balance rate of 8%. He warned that the flat rate is actually much more expensive because you pay interest on the full amount even as you pay it back. He also checked a credit card statement, noting that the interest-free period only applies if you pay the full bill, not just a part of it. We then calculated interest for a six-month loan. Since the formula uses time in years, we had to use 0.5 years, not 6, to get the correct amount. Finally, he explained that while a 10-year loan has a smaller monthly EMI, you end up paying much more in total interest than with a 2-year loan. I realized that borrowing is not just about the interest rate or the monthly payment; it is about the total cost over time. I must always check the fine print before agreeing to any loan or using a credit card.
response.summary: The passage explains that loan costs depend on how interest is calculated and the duration of the loan. It highlights that flat rates and long tenures often lead to higher total payments. It also clarifies that credit card benefits require full payment of the bill.
